name: List Replicability Number
definition: A learner is **$(\epsilon,L)$-list replicable** for $\mathcal H$ if, for every $\delta>0$, some sample size makes its output lie with probability at least $1-\delta$ in a fixed list of $L$ hypotheses, all of error below $\epsilon$, for every realizable distribution. Let $\mathrm{LR}(\mathcal H,\epsilon)$ be the least such $L$ and define the **list replicability number** $\mathrm{LR}(\mathcal H)=\lim_{\epsilon\to0}\mathrm{LR}(\mathcal H,\epsilon)$.
graph_summary: Smallest eventual list size to which a randomized learner’s output can be confined while remaining accurate.
description: A realizable PAC-learning stability parameter; its definition includes the accuracy limit $\epsilon\to0$.
origin_references: Defined in the list-replicability framework used by \cite{chornomaz2025spherical}.

monotonic.proof: Any $(\epsilon,L)$-list-replicable learner for $\mathcal H$ also works for a subclass: every distribution realizable by the subclass is realizable by $\mathcal H$, so the same learner, sample size, and distribution-dependent accurate list apply. Minimize $L$ and take the accuracy limit.

p_monotonic.proof: Let $\mathcal R=\mathcal H_{|S}$. Run an $(\epsilon,L)$-list-replicable learner for $\mathcal H$ on a distribution supported on the retained coordinates and restrict every output hypothesis and every member of its fixed list to $S$. Every target in $\mathcal R$ has an extension in $\mathcal H$; restriction preserves its error on the supported distribution and cannot enlarge the list. Minimize $L$ and take the accuracy limit.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is a restriction to a subfamily followed by a coordinate projection, so the established subfamily and projection monotonicities imply this form.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding arguments establish monotonicity under both subfamilies and coordinate projections.
